section: A29 rehearsal 3 — two instances against the merged parity — 2026-09-08
headline: Two isolated Vidra instances at schema 142 on merged main (the A29 parity work of core #210 / user #202 plus core #209), behind a real Caddy reproducing deploy/Caddyfile sections 1, 2, 3, 3a and 4. The parity section wrote this run a checklist; the run measured every line of it and found FIVE defects, four of them in clauses that section claimed and no HTTP client had ever exercised.

lab.scheme: plain HTTP; no TLS anywhere. Caddy runs with `auto_https off` on two http:// site addresses, so §3a routing is exercised without an internal CA.
lab.edge: REAL Caddy v2.11.4 (brew, `caddy run --config`), ONE config with two site blocks mirroring deploy/Caddyfile sections 1, 2, 3, 3a and 4 verbatim in structure — the /metrics and /api/v1/dev/* 404s, the @api path list, the @ap_object / @ap_object_ld Accept matchers above the frontend fallthrough, `encode zstd gzip` scoped to the frontend block. Only site addresses and upstreams differ. `caddy validate` passed before every run.
lab.hostnames: NONE ADDED — /etc/hosts needs root. The two instances are distinguished by PORT and their fediverse domains are literally `127.0.0.1:18080` and `127.0.0.1:28080`.
lab.third_party_peer: one instance of docs/evidence/a29-ap-peer.go — `commenter` on :48080, the source of every unsigned/tampered/stolen-keyId/spoofed-actor probe and of the third-instance comment. Throwaway key under /tmp, never committed.
lab.one_build_two_origins: ONE `next build` of vidra-user, served by both frontends with different INTERNAL_API_BASE_URL and PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL; NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL was never baked. Rebuilt once mid-run to carry the threaded-mirror fix.
lab.infrastructure: PostgreSQL 16.15 (Homebrew, native, own cluster on 127.0.0.1:55471, socket -k /tmp), Redis 8.6.2 on 127.0.0.1:56411, ffmpeg 8.1, six-second 640x360 fixtures, Node 26.8.1 for both frontends, Go 1.26.2 binaries, Playwright 1.62.1's real Chromium. No Docker.

code_under_test.vidra-core: origin/main b7f5c45 (schema 142: the A29 parity migration 0142 merged) for the first pass of every clause; then a29/rehearsal-3 91abfe2 and 542b0f3 (vidra-core #215) for the re-measurement of the four clauses those commits fix. The section says which reading is which.

HTTP_IMPORT_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=true on both — the only knob that lets urlsafety.Guard reach a loopback origin.

POST /api/v1/channels {handle: CreatorA} — same name, different case

sc1_namespace_and_webfinger.backfill_on_a_seeded_pre_existing_collis: Instance A was migrated to 142, rolled back to 141 (0142's own down SQL + `migrate force 141 --yes-i-know`), seeded with the collision the API can no longer create — user `creatora`, channel `creatora`, and channel `creatora-channel` already taken — then migrated up. Result: the channel renamed to `creatora-channel-2` (the first candidate was taken), the ACCOUNT kept `creatora`, one audit row `content.channel.handle_renamed` reason `from=creatora to=creatora-channel-2` with both names in metadata and `cause=handle_namespace_backfill`, and one `channel_handle_aliases` row `creatora` with `is_actor_id=true` and `expires_at` one year out.

acct:creatora-channel-2@127.0.0.1:18080 (the renamed channel by its NEW name)

sc1_namespace_and_webfinger.frozen_actor_id: GET /video-channels/creatora with Accept: application/activity+json → 200, type Group, id/inbox/outbox/followers/publicKey.id ALL at `…/video-channels/creatora`, preferredUsername `creatora-channel-2`. The id did not follow the rename; only the display name did.

defect_1_human_301.on merged main: FAIL. GET /api/v1/channels/creatora answered 404. `GetChannelHandleAlias` had exactly ONE caller — internal/federation/actor.go — so the FEDERATED half of the alias worked and the HUMAN half described in the migration's own comment and in the register was never wired.
defect_1_human_301.on vidra-core #215: PASS, measured through Caddy: 301 with `Location: /api/v1/channels/creatora-channel-2`, following it 200; the current handle 200; a handle nothing was renamed from 404.

defect_2_follow_picks_the_person.on merged main: FAIL, twice over. B followed `creatora@127.0.0.1:18080` and stored `…/accounts/creatora`: `fetchWebFinger` returns only the rel=self link, so the two-link answer 0142 shipped had no client that could read it. The Follow was delivered 202 to the Person and the row sat `pending` — exactly the request the second rehearsal watched.
defect_2_follow_picks_the_person.second_half: Even addressed correctly the Follow was dropped: `handleFollow`, `handleUndo`, `ChannelCollection` and `ChannelOutboxPage` all resolved the path handle with a plain `GetChannelByHandle`, so an activity aimed at the FROZEN actor id — the only address existing peers hold for a renamed channel — found no channel. Answered 202 and recorded nothing.
defect_2_follow_picks_the_person.on vidra-core #215: PASS end to end: B stored `…/video-channels/creatora`, reported the handle `creatora-channel-2@127.0.0.1:18080`, A resolved the renamed channel and Accepted, and both sides read `accepted` within 20 s. `/video-channels/creatora/followers` answers `totalItems: 1` with its id at the frozen handle, and the outbox at the frozen id answers 200.

sc2_account_scoped_block.verdict: PASS on merged main for every hiding rule; the audit trail FAILED and passes only on vidra-core #215
sc2_account_scoped_block.topology: B follows A's `studioa` (owned by `creatora`) and A's `newsroom` (owned by `ownera`). Both channels' videos mirror onto B, and A's local thread mirrors with them, so B holds `creatora`'s comments on BOTH videos and `ownera`'s on both.

matrix.columns: videos visible in GET /videos/search?q=clip | authors visible in the studioa thread | authors visible in the newsroom thread

baseline.viewerb: Lab clip two, Newsroom clip | creatora, ownera | ownera, creatora

sc2_account_scoped_block.what_the_matrix_proves: The block names the ACCOUNT and reaches the channel: `studioa`'s video left the blocker's surfaces while `newsroom`'s stayed, and `creatora`'s already-stored comments left BOTH threads — including the one on a video belonging to a channel `creatora` does not own. `remote_actor_block_reach` held two rows for the one block: `…/accounts/creatora` and `…/video-channels/studioa`.
sc2_account_scoped_block.retroactivity: Every comment hidden was posted BEFORE the block. Nothing was deleted to hide it; the unblock restored the identical rows.
sc2_account_scoped_block.chromium: Signed in as viewerb on B's remote watch page for A's video (Playwright 1.62.1). The page offers Report / Block account / Mute instance; the control's accessible name is `Block studioa@127.0.0.1:18080` and its POST /api/v1/me/blocks/remote sends `http://127.0.0.1:18080/accounts/creatora` — the OWNING ACCOUNT, per the ruling. After the click the page reads 'Blocked studioa@127.0.0.1:18080. Their videos and replies no longer appear for you — on this instance. They can still see yours.' Unblock restored every row.

defect_3_audit_rows_never_persisted.on merged main: FAIL. The admin block and unblock both answered 204 and wrote ZERO rows. The handler put the actor URL in `resource_id`; the audit envelope refuses one there ('resource_id must be a bounded opaque identifier, not a URL or payload'), `Record` returned an error, and the persist is best-effort by design — a WARN line in the log and nothing else. The parity section's claim that these actions write `moderation.remote_actor.block` / `.unblock` was architecturally impossible under the envelope's own rules.
defect_3_audit_rows_never_persisted.on vidra-core #215: PASS: two rows, `moderation.remote_actor.block` and `.unblock`, `resource_type=remote_actor`, `reason=actor=http://127.0.0.1:18080/accounts/creatora`, `result=success`, `actor_role=admin` — the same shape the sibling `moderation.instance.block` has always used (`domain=<host>`).

sc2_account_scoped_block.drift_not_a_defect: The parity table says an inbound `Create{Note}` from a viewer-blocked actor is REFUSED. Measured: it is STORED and filtered per viewer. `IsRemoteActorBlockedByAnyone` is only a gate that hands the decision to the caller, and storing-then-filtering is the better behaviour — one viewer's block must not censor the instance's copy for everyone. The table is what is wrong, not the code.

sc3_instance_block_and_f4_redelivery.verdict: PARTIAL — the block, the audit row, the cancellation, the F4 video redelivery and the percent-encoded unblock all PASS; a Follow refused by a block strands the SENDER at `pending` forever, and a cancelled comment is never resumed
timeline: 16:44:29 B's api killed (Caddy 502). creatora comments on A; three deliveries queue and start failing.
16:45:01 A's admin blocks instance 127.0.0.1:28080. 204. Audit row `moderation.instance.block reason=domain=127.0.0.1:28080` PERSISTED.
16:45:26–16:45:46 all three deliveries reach `failed` with `cancelled: destination instance is blocked`. Cancellation is lazy — it happens when the delivery next comes due, not at block time.
16:45:35 B's api restored; a NEW user on B follows A's studioa. A's inbox refuses it: audit row `federation.inbox.rejected reason=domain=127.0.0.1:28080` at 16:45:44. B's delivery is 202/delivered.

16:46:20 A unblocks with `DELETE /admin/instances/blocked/127.0.0.1%3A28080` — the PERCENT-ENCODED colon — 204. Redelivery requeued 0: the cancelled rows were comment Creates, and they are outside this block's window anyway.
16:46:54 second block, this time with a VIDEO published during it. Create ×3 at 16:46:54 and the transcode-completion Update ×3 at 16:47:04 all cancelled by 16:47:11.
16:47:18 unblock. Log: `resumed outbound deliveries cancelled while the instance was blocked domain=127.0.0.1:28080 requeued=6`.
16:47:26 all six delivered. B holds EXACTLY ONE `remote_videos` row for the video (3 Creates + 3 Updates converge on the object_url upsert).
sc3_instance_block_and_f4_redelivery.defect_4_comment_creates_are_never_resum: Measured inside a clean block window: a `Create{Note}` cancelled by the block is left cancelled on unblock. `redeliverable` resolves a Create/Update's object to a LOCAL VIDEO id (`<baseURL>/videos/<uuid>`); a comment's object id is `<baseURL>/comments/<uuid>`, so it falls to the conservative default. The follower's mirrored thread is permanently short every comment written during a block — the same shape of permanent divergence F4 exists to close for videos. NOT FIXED here; it needs the same existence-and-visibility check one level down, and a ruling on whether a comment on a still-public video qualifies.
sc3_instance_block_and_f4_redelivery.defect_5_a_refused_follow_strands_the_se: B's Follow, refused by A's instance block, left B's `remote_channel_follows` row `pending` and there it stays. A answers 202 and drops (deliberately — a Reject would confirm the block), B's own delivery succeeded, and nothing on either side ever re-attempts or expires the row. This is the clause this run was told to prove and it does not pass. It is a RULING, not a patch: either a block emits a Reject (which A29-F5's `severingActivity` rule already exempts from cancellation, and which tells the blocked instance it is blocked), or the sender expires its own pending follows. Neither was invented here.
sc3_instance_block_and_f4_redelivery.the_reject_path_itself_passes: Separately measured with `federation_allow_channel_followers` off on A: B's follow went `rejected` (terminal, creator-visible in GET /me/remote-follows), and re-following re-armed it to `pending` with a NEW Follow activity id (`…/activities/follow/2` → `…/follow/9`). The parity fix (b) works; it simply has no arm for the case where the refusal sends nothing.

sc4_threaded_mirror.verdict: PASS for the clause as written — with the RENDERING half fixed on vidra-user #205
timeline: creatora posts a top-level comment on A's public video → mirrored on B at depth 0 within seconds.
ownera replies to it on A → mirrored on B with `parent_object_url` = creatora's comment object id.
creatora replies to ownera's reply → mirrored on B at depth 2, `parent_object_url` = ownera's comment.
creatora EDITS the top-level comment on A → B's row updates (`edited=t`, new body) within ~10 s.
creatora DELETES the depth-2 reply on A → it disappears from B's mirror within ~12 s.
sc4_threaded_mirror.defect_6_the_page_rendered_it_flat: The data threads; the page did not. In Chromium every mirrored row rendered at depth 0 with 0px of indent and no 'replying to' text — a real reply sat beside the comment it answered as if unrelated. `RemoteVideoThread` never read `parent_object_url`. Fixed on vidra-user #205 and re-measured in Chromium: the reply renders at `data-thread-depth=1` with 16px of indent and a 'Replying to creatora' line.
sc4_threaded_mirror.newly_measured_hole: A reply whose PARENT is a third instance's comment is delivered and dropped. The lab's peer at :48080 posted a Note on A's video; A stored it and did NOT fan it out (AnnounceComment is a no-op for remote-authored comments, so this instance never re-broadcasts content signed by another server). A's creator then replied to it, and the Create carried `inReplyTo: http://127.0.0.1:48080/notes/1` — a parent B had never been sent. `resolveMirrorThread` resolves inReplyTo to a remote video or an already-stored mirrored comment; neither matched, so B stored nothing while A's ledger read `delivered`. Every follower's mirror therefore has a hole at the top of any thread a third instance started, and everything under it is silently lost. Not a regression and not fixed here: re-broadcasting a Note this instance cannot sign is an Announce-shaped design change, not a patch.
sc4_threaded_mirror.f8_authoring: STILL THE RESIDUAL, and now explicit rather than merely absent. There is no POST route for a mirrored thread; `internal/httpapi/remote_video_comments.go` says so in its own words — 'READ-ONLY, and the absence of a POST is the design rather than an omission… Authoring a comment against a video hosted elsewhere reverses a shipped product decision and raises a moderation question mirroring does not' — and the watch page tells the reader the same thing. This is why the run's block matrix is taken on B against an account on A rather than the other way round: B's users cannot author onto A's video at all.

sc6_mig06_and_regression.mig06_identity_clause: STILL UNVERIFIED, unchanged and deliberately not faked. Source identity after a migration needs actor-`id` continuity, key continuity or a `Move`, which `dispatchActivity` still has no arm for. What 0142 freezes is an id across a RENAME on one instance, which is a different promise from an identity that survives moving hosts.
sc6_mig06_and_regression.regression: vidra-core `make ci` PASS (fmt-check, vet, migrate-lint at 142, openapi-verify, sqlc-verify, test-race) on both commits of #215; `ci-required` SUCCESS on head 542b0f3. vidra-user: typecheck PASS, lint 0 errors / 2 pre-existing warnings, lint:icons PASS, 2598 vitest tests in 259 files PASS, `next build` PASS, and the FULL Playwright suite **627 passed**. Every code change is TDD: each defect got a failing test first, and each test names the lab observation it encodes.

defects_found: GET /api/v1/channels/{old} answered 404, not the 301 the migration comment and the register both promise — the alias had one caller. FIXED vidra-core #215.
moderation.remote_actor.block / .unblock persisted NOTHING: an actor URL in resource_id is refused by the audit envelope and the persist is best-effort. FIXED vidra-core #215.
Following a shared handle queued the Follow at the Person: the two-link WebFinger answer 0142 ships had no client that reads it. FIXED vidra-core #215.

Inbound activity addressed at a renamed channel's FROZEN actor id was answered 202 and dropped — handleFollow, handleUndo and both collection routes could not see the alias, so the id this instance advertises addressed a channel none of them could find. FIXED vidra-core #215.
The mirrored thread rendered FLAT in the browser despite carrying parent_object_url. FIXED vidra-user #205.
OPEN: a Create{Note} cancelled by an instance block is never resumed on unblock (F4 covers videos only).
OPEN: a Follow refused by an instance block leaves the SENDER's row `pending` forever — needs a ruling, not a patch.
OPEN: a reply whose parent is a THIRD instance's comment is delivered and dropped, because this instance never re-broadcasts remote-authored comments.
OPEN, cosmetic: the remote watch page's block control is named for the CHANNEL (`Block studioa@…`) while it blocks the ACCOUNT and every channel it owns.
OPEN, cosmetic: /admin/system reports block-cancelled deliveries as 'dead_lettered' with the message 'one or more peers did not accept what it sent'.

OPEN, product: migration 0142's backfill mints handles containing a hyphen (`<h>-channel-2`), which the channel-handle validator refuses ('must be 3–30 chars: letters, digits, or underscore'). Reads work, so nothing is broken today, but the instance cannot re-create such a handle and the rename rule and the validator disagree.

gates.vidra-user-trap: A trap worth recording: the e2e suite fails 7 tests against a build made WITHOUT `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL`. The lab needs a build with no baked base URL (both origins are served from one bundle through runtime PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL); `npm run ci` bakes `http://localhost:8080`, and hls/watch/about assert the absolute src. The failures reproduce identically on unmodified origin/main files, so they say nothing about the change — they say the tree still held the LAB build. Rebuilt with the ci env: 627/627.
